summary: Connected curation of all 31 selected water, restoration-monitoring and drone pages, preserving source contexts.

findings.label: Drones can support restoration monitoring
findings.text: The manual suggests high-resolution drone imagery to improve vegetation monitoring. This concerns observation, not irrigation delivery.

findings.label: Monitor several kinds of ground cover
findings.text: Distinguish herbaceous cover, woody cover, remains/rocks and bare soil. Fixed transects and location records support repeat measurements.

findings.label: A dated land-cover example in Portugal
findings.text: A pictured example uses KNN classification on 2021 Sentinel 2 imagery around Carregal do Sal.

findings.label: Plan supply and water-harvesting effects together
findings.text: Water availability affects methods, quantities and frequency. The manual also considers runoff captured by planting techniques, naming Cocoon and microbasins.

findings.label: Use suitable amendments in suitable amounts
findings.text: The manual suggests organic amendments for nourishment, biological activity and water holding. It calls for low pollutants, no impurities, stable material and avoiding excessive doses; examples are 1–2 L/planting hole or 50 Mg/ha surface application, retaining those different application contexts.

findings.label: Choose the method for the actual site
findings.text: Species, climate, soil, water availability/quality, topography, costs, resources, access and environmental effects matter. Biodiversity, monitoring and future resilience are also included, without selecting one universal best technique.

findings.label: Choose native combinations for habitat objectives
findings.text: Where restoration aims to recover habitat and biodiversity, the manual advises techniques and species combinations that encourage native species and diverse habitat for local flora and fauna. It does not prescribe a particular beneficial carob companion combination.

findings.label: Restoration methods should follow explicit objectives
findings.text: The manual names protecting soils/ecosystems, stabilizing pollution, carbon sequestration, timber production and leisure among possible reforestation objectives. It calls for explicit project objectives and suitable species/methods rather than assuming the same purpose everywhere.

findings.label: Allow establishment before severe weather
findings.text: The manual discusses moderate temperatures and adequate rainfall, with generic early-spring/monsoon examples. Local Mediterranean dates are not computed from these generic examples.

findings.label: The LIFE control used holes and pipe watering
findings.text: The method uses 40×40×40 cm holes, no additional tillage and a stated minimum 1.50 m spacing. Shallow/stony areas need adaptation. These are project-method details, not a planting layout for a new site.

findings.label: Traditional-method summary has its own scope
findings.text: The summary reports 3,002 planted trees,33% survival,53 L/tree and €136/surviving tree. It remains distinct from the dated July 2023 table, whose denominators and values differ.

aspects.Scope: Method summary, distinct from dated table

findings.label: LIFE describes a 20 L Cocoon
findings.text: The manual describes a buried biodegradable reservoir initially filled with 20 L, near-root delivery and shelter. These are source-described functions; trial outcomes and additional watering remain separate.

findings.label: Cocoon is not a no-watering guarantee
findings.text: An introductory passage describes reduced regular watering, but the next page includes initial base water,20 L reservoir fill and further irrigation if necessary; management guidance also describes summer watering.

findings.label: Humidity and slope can limit placement
findings.text: The manual advises against very humid sites because deterioration can accelerate; steep placement can incline reservoirs and spill water.

findings.label: Cocoon is described as single-use
findings.text: The source says no reuse is possible and describes degradation in soil. It reports €7.80 per unit for LIFE; this is a historical source-stated cost, not a current quote.

findings.label: Cocoon summary has its own scope
findings.text: The method summary reports 1,993 planted trees,68% survival,49 L/tree and €109/surviving tree. It is preserved separately from the later dated results table.

aspects.Scope: Method summary, distinct from dated table

findings.label: Fog collectors combine moisture collection and shelter
findings.text: The manual describes 25×25 mm steel mesh and 3×3 mm PE Russell mesh, collecting water by condensation/impact and providing shade/wind cover. It reports qualitatively better survival with PE mesh; no numeric rate is given on this page.

findings.label: Fog collectors still need suitable sites and water
findings.text: Good fog collection conditions are primary. First-year watering and moisture checks are still described, with quantities dependent on site and species.

findings.label: A source-described pipe and hose network
findings.text: The installation example describes 32-diameter branches,19 mm valve connections every 25 m and 19 mm hoses with quick connections. The source explicitly says project requirements, topography and equipment change details.

findings.label: Keep four types of water distinct
findings.text: Nursery, settlement, maintenance and support water have different purposes. Soil, rainfall and species affect quantity/frequency.

findings.label: Settlement water is additional to the reservoir fill
findings.text: The LIFE choices describe roughly 10–15 L settlement water per seedling across methods, with a further 20 L reservoir fill for Cocoon.

findings.label: LIFE summer schedules are project-specific
findings.text: The manual describes 15 L/plant monthly July–September for traditional/Cocoon and 10 L for IND. These are project schedules, not universal requirements.

findings.label: Use weather and plant condition to consider support water
findings.text: Inspect forecasts and plants: prolonged dryness or widespread yellow/dry symptoms may justify additional watering.

findings.label: Dated LIFE water-use comparison
findings.text: On 26 July 2023 the table gives water/surviving tree: traditional 133.5 L, Cocoon 57.4 L, i-FWC 35.3 L, AFDS 101.4 L; survival proportions 0.43,0.87,0.89,0.83 respectively. This project snapshot is not a prediction for Maysara or another site.

findings.label: The manual reports savings against a control estimate
findings.text: The manual reports 509,495 L overall reduction against a traditional-method counterfactual. This is a source indicator, not a new-project forecast; component values have a one-litre sum discrepancy.

findings.label: Interpret pilots with disturbances and conditions
findings.text: The report evaluates survival/growth alongside rain, irrigation, soil texture/rockiness, seedling quality, soil preparation, management, weeds and reservoir damage. Some datasets were corrected or excluded.

findings.label: Al Faisal carob was lost to flooding
findings.text: All fall carob plants were destroyed by canal floods and not replanted. Empty carob cells are missing results following disturbance, not a measured zero-survival Cocoon efficacy comparison.

findings.label: Al Faisal olive refill was comparable to irrigation
findings.text: At May 2020 monitoring, olive survival was 93.9% with Cocoon refill,92.0% without Cocoon/with irrigation and 72.9% Cocoon/no-refill. The source regards refill/irrigation performance as similar and the no-refill deficit as significant.

findings.label: Al Faisal olive water schedules differ
findings.text: Table 5.2 reports 50 L Cocoon refill water (initial/emergency) versus 1,080 L no-Cocoon irrigation (initial/emergency/weekly-to-biweekly summer water) over May 2019–May 2020. Preserve schedule and site when comparing volumes.

findings.label: Al Faisal almond survival remained low
findings.text: Both reported almond comparison treatments had 36.0% survival. The authors discuss dry-summer sensitivity and better-planned water supply; this is not universal device failure.

findings.label: Growth comparisons depend on species and period
findings.text: May 2020 mean olive heights: 98.0 cm Cocoon refill,86.3 cm no-refill,85.1 cm no-Cocoon irrigation. Olive refill differences were significant; almond/pine height differences were not. Pine had only 3–4 months growth after replacement.

findings.label: Emergency water changed Maysara comparisons
findings.text: Spring Cocoon scenarios were refilled twice in unexpectedly hot summer 2019; no-Cocoon/no-irrigation seedlings also received water. Those original comparison labels were excluded. January 2021 monitoring was not used because watering information was incomplete.

findings.label: Carob survival was poor in the Maysara spring trial
findings.text: May 2019 planting assessed May 2020: 1.0% carob survival with Cocoon refill (95% CI 0.2–5.5),2.0% no-Cocoon irrigation (95% CI 0.6–7.1). No significant treatment difference was found. Poor results were attributed mainly to summer dryness and very poor sandy-soil water retention.

aspects.Conditions: Late spring; hot summer; poor sandy-soil retention

findings.label: Water totals did not guarantee Maysara survival
findings.text: Table 5.5 reports 75 L initial/emergency Cocoon fills and 510 L initial/follow-up no-Cocoon irrigation for carob during May 2019–May 2020. Survival remained poor under the reported conditions.

findings.label: Fall results concern other species and a short period
findings.text: Fall pine/acacia performed better with winter rain and composting. Cocoon/no-refill survival was 100% for both; no-Cocoon/no-irrigation 94.4% pine and 72.5% acacia. The period since December 2019 was only five months. These are not fall carob results.

findings.label: Retain original carob spellings with one checked identity
findings.text: Several passages/tables use Ceratonia silique, while Table 5.1 prints Ceratonia siliqua and labels it carob. Preserve the original wording linked to checked carob; infer no naming authority from a variant spelling.

findings.label: The supplier annex describes about 25 L
findings.text: The Land Life Company annex describes wax-sealed recycled pulp/cardboard reservoir/lid and shelter; approximate 25 L fill and 1–3 months discharge depend on soil/climate. Rain/runoff can recharge it. This differs from LIFE 20 L wording.

findings.label: Dry summers can require additional Cocoon water
findings.text: MENAQUA suggests refilling at an appropriate summer time and a removable access cover. This regional guidance does not promise one fill is sufficient.

findings.label: Inspect reservoir condition after planting
findings.text: Monitor damage/degradation. Snow can damage lids and freezing can damage pulp walls; seasonal lid removal/replacement is a source suggestion for snow conditions.

findings.label: Observed roots differ from intended deep rooting
findings.text: The report notes roots tending horizontally below reservoirs and identifies downward rooting as an open issue. The supplier annex describes deep rooting as intended function. Preserve these as different statements.

findings.label: Degradation time depends on environment
findings.text: The report says experience with moderate rainfall was breakup in 1.5–2 years, but leaves semi-arid duration open. It suggests reservoir strengthening for wind, runoff, soil pressure and frost.

findings.label: Cocoon requires suitable soil and species
findings.text: Supplier guidance: at least 30 cm topsoil; clear piercing rocks from top 25 cm; preferably deep medium-textured subsoil with replenished water; check salinity/chemistry for the species. A planting tool cannot make an unsuitable tree locally adapted.

findings.label: Healthy roots and planting material remain essential
findings.text: Supplier prefers trees under one year, containers at most 4 L and diameter under 15 cm, healthy shoots/roots and no serious circling/J-rooting. Shoots preferably under 40 cm; avoid voids around the root ball. These are supplier criteria, not independent efficacy results.

findings.label: Mycorrhiza is a supplier-described option
findings.text: The annex suggests nursery/planting inoculation to improve access to moisture/nutrients; selected pages do not report a controlled inoculation result.

findings.label: Monitor growth and vigor with their limitations
findings.text: The annex describes height, base stem diameter and vigor. Grazing can cause apparent negative height growth; shelters obstruct diameter measurement. First-year establishment is distinguished from later drought, grazing/fire effects.

findings.label: Keep the printed conclusion date distinct
findings.text: The selected conclusion page is signed The Hague,11 January 2022; the library filename uses 2021-12. Retain each date with its meaning.

findings.label: The study sprayed citrus canopies with water
findings.text: The study sought orchard spray delivery from continuous ground supplies. Tests used water; pesticide tests were future work. It did not measure seedling establishment, root-zone irrigation or carob survival.

findings.label: Reported experimental aircraft specifications
findings.text: Table 1 describes a 2100×2100×450 mm hexacopter,12 kg airframe,24 kg maximum takeoff mass and six 24-inch propellers. These describe the experiment, not a purchase recommendation or operating authorization.

findings.label: The drone has a concrete supply chain
findings.text: The setup combines Cube Black/custom ArduCopter, RTK base/rover, Mission Planner, ground engine pump, hose/nozzle and 200 V AC→300 V DC transmission→48 V aircraft supply. These are browsable source-described components.

findings.label: Tilting propellers counter spray recoil
findings.text: Propeller surfaces tilt instead of the entire aircraft to produce horizontal thrust. The study reports stable posture and positioning during spraying.

findings.label: Automatic trial: Innoshima,19 September 2023
findings.text: With Sanwa Farm the aircraft followed an automatic route on sloping orchard terrain; takeoff/landing were manual to avoid fence/hose/cable entanglement.

findings.label: Manual trial: Ikuchijima,20 September 2023
findings.text: With Harada Farm, manual PosHold flight sprayed trees. A crawler UGV carried cable/hose and was designed to follow beyond 5 m separation.

findings.label: Water-sensitive paper showed spray adhesion
findings.text: Paper in the trees recorded spray deposition with several adhesion indices of 10; the authors conclude water adhered well. This does not establish soil wetting, irrigation efficiency or tree survival.

findings.label: Experiment and publication dates differ
findings.text: Experiments occurred September 2023. The article records receipt 6 March 2024 and publication 21 March 2024.

findings.label: The authors identify a project framework
findings.text: The research was carried out under the 2023 Hiroshima Smart Agriculture Project for an integrated large-scale lemon/other-crop system. This is context, not funding eligibility for another project.
